subject: Ridley Scott
hook: Why did Apple try to sell its most famous ad?
twist: The ad Apple's board hated and tried to sell off, which aired once in the Super Bowl, became the most remembered ad of all.
mood: Cold 1980s blue-grey dystopian airbrush, grain and scanlines, with a single warm accent: the glint on a sledgehammer. Music: slow brooding analog synth pulse at about 80 bpm, low drones and a sparse arpeggio, lifting to a bright metallic hit on the twist.
narration: Why did Apple try to sell its most famous ad? In December nineteen eighty-three, Apple's board watched the new Macintosh commercial. Chief executive John Sculley later said most felt it was the worst commercial they had seen. The director was Ridley Scott, fresh from Blade Runner. He filmed it in England, casting local skinheads as the shaven, grey workers. Sculley told the agency, Chiat Day, to sell the airtime. It sold thirty seconds and said it was too late for the rest. Steve Wozniak says he even offered to pay half the airtime himself. So the full ad aired once, during the Super Bowl on January twenty-second, nineteen eighty-four. The ad Apple tried to sell is now the one everyone remembers. Bold gamble, or lucky escape?

In December 1983, Apple's board watched Ridley Scott's new Macintosh commercial. John Sculley later said most of them felt it was the worst commercial they had seen.

Sculley told the agency, Chiat/Day, to sell the airtime. It sold thirty seconds and said it was too late for the rest. Steve Wozniak says he offered to pay half the airtime himself.

So the full ad aired once, during the Super Bowl on January 22, 1984. The ad Apple tried to sell is the one everyone remembers.
